actors.description: Male bowler viewed from behind on the right side of the frame, standing on the approach of a multi-lane PBA tournament center. He wears a black short-sleeved collared shirt with 'ZACH WILKINS' in light lettering across the upper back, dark trousers, dark shoes and a dark cap. He carries and delivers a reddish/pink-orange bowling ball with one hand (one_handed support).

shots.storyline: One continuous, slightly drifting shot looks diagonally down a row of oiled lanes (overhead rail numbers 12–18) inside a PBA event, with a large white 'Gene Carter's Pro Shop Classic' banner at upper-left, a black date strip 'AUG 16-18, 2019' and a 'THIS IS BOWLING' strip across the top, vertical player pennants (JONES, DAUGHERTY, ARCHER, TEECE, PRATHER, TACKETT) hanging above the pin decks, and a partially cut-off white schedule/scoring board at the far-left edge. The bowler S01-P01 stands nearly motionless at the right-side approach, ball held low at his side, watching the lanes from 0.0 s to about 3.5 s. Around 3.6 s he begins his approach, translating up-screen and drifting toward screen-left along the lane perspective toward the foul line; he bends at the waist as the ball drops into the backswing (≈4.5–4.9 s), swings it forward (≈4.9–5.2 s) while his front foot slides into delivery, and at ≈5.3 s the hand opens so the ball separates and starts independent travel up-screen/screen-left down the lane (visible rolling from ≈5.4 s). He holds a one_handed follow-through with the throwing arm extended up/forward and the trailing leg kicked high behind (finish_leg trailing_lifted) through ≈5.4–6.6 s, then gradually lowers the pose and stands watching (≈7.2–8.0 s, a held stance outside the action inventory). Pin scatter is visible at the left pin decks near 7.7–8.3 s (not an athlete technique). From ≈8.0 s he pivots away from the lane, rotating toward screen-left to face back toward the seating area, and begins walking off the approach; the shot ends mid-turn at 8.567 s, cropping the recovery. Camera framing drifts subtly right-to-left over the clip, progressively revealing the TEECE/PRATHER pennants, the lane-12 rail number, and more of the left schedule board.

actions.evidence: After a near-held stance (0.0–3.5 s) with only minor weight shifts, the bowler takes forward steps; his body translates up-screen and drifts toward screen-left along the lane perspective toward the foul line, ball carried low at the side. First clear step ≈3.6 s; arrival at the slide/foul-line area ≈4.5 s.
actions.detail: Approach walk from the waiting stance into the delivery area; movement is away from the camera (up-screen) with a screen-left drift following the lane axis. The start boundary is estimated because the pre-3.6 s posture is essentially static.

actions.evidence: Torso flexes forward and the ball travels rearward/downward behind the body, reaching the rear apex ≈4.9 s as he bends at the waist (frames 4.6–4.9 show the ball low behind the sliding foot).
actions.detail: One_handed backswing; ball moves from the side carry to a low rear position behind the body.

actions.evidence: Front foot plants and glides on the approach surface into the delivery crouch, overlapping the backswing/forward-swing window (≈4.5–5.2 s); body lowers and rotates toward the lane.
actions.detail: Final sliding step of the approach; the slide finish coincides with the ball reaching the ankle at the start of release.

actions.evidence: Ball swings forward from the rear apex toward the lane, passing the body at ankle/foot level by ≈5.2 s (frames 5.0–5.2).
actions.detail: One_handed forward swing accelerating the ball toward the release point.

actions.evidence: Hand opens and the ball separates from the fingers at ≈5.3 s, beginning independent travel; the ball is visible on the lane from ≈5.4 s rolling up-screen/screen-left toward the pin decks.
actions.detail: Release at the slide; ball trajectory is away from the camera down the lane, converging toward the left-side pin decks in this diagonal perspective.

actions.evidence: Throwing arm stays extended up/forward and the trailing leg is kicked high behind (trailing_lifted) through ≈5.4–6.6 s, then the pose gradually lowers as he watches the ball; arm/leg return toward neutral by ≈7.2 s.
actions.detail: One_handed delivery with finish_leg trailing_lifted; body leans into the lane while the ball continues down-screen. The held watching stance after ≈7.2 s is not part of the technique.

actions.evidence: Bowler pivots away from the lane, rotating toward screen-left into a left profile (glasses visible), and starts walking back off the approach; the turn is still in progress when the shot ends, so the recovery is cropped at the boundary.
actions.detail: Post-delivery recovery/turn-away, not a delivery technique; body rotation is toward screen-left, movement back down-screen toward the seating area.

uncertainties: Exact lane number used by the bowler is ambiguous: the diagonal camera perspective makes the ball's down-lane path appear to align with the left pin decks (13/14) while the bowler stands at the right-side approach (≈16/17).
The precise instant of the first approach step is estimated (≈3.6 s); the 0.0–3.5 s posture is a near-held stance with only minor adjustments, so the approach start boundary is approximate.
Pin fall/count at the far deck (≈7.7–8.3 s) is observable but excluded from athlete techniques per the inventory; whether the delivery was a strike or a leave cannot be confirmed from these frames.
Left-edge schedule-board text is partially cut off and only intermittently legible; transcribed fragments may be incomplete.
The TEECE and PRATHER pennant letterings become fully legible only as the bowler steps away and the framing drifts; their exact reveal times (≈3.0–3.8 s) are approximate.
The final turn/walk-back is cropped by the shot end at 8.567 s, so its full extent and final facing direction are not completely observed.

action_sounds.description: No distinguishable approach footfalls; only the continuous ambient hum and indistinct chatter during 3.6-4.5 s.
action_sounds.evidence: Audio across the approach window contains only the sustained background bed with no discrete transients aligned to his steps; visible footfalls alone are not evidence of sound.

action_sounds.description: No audible sound attributable to the backswing.
action_sounds.evidence: The backswing is a silent body motion; no transient occurs in 4.5-4.9 s beyond the ambient bed.

action_sounds.description: Slide plant/glide not separately audible; the only nearby transient (5.16-5.36 s) aligns with ball release rather than the ~4.6 s plant.
action_sounds.evidence: No discrete squeak or thud can be localized to the slide; the tap occurs roughly 0.6 s after the plant moment.

action_sounds.description: Forward swing produces no distinguishable sound.
action_sounds.evidence: Swing is silent; ambient-only audio until the release transient.

action_sounds.description: Single sharp tap/click as the ball leaves the hand and contacts the lane.
action_sounds.evidence: A lone transient at 5.16-5.36 s coincides with frame-verified ball separation (~5.3 s) and first lane contact; no competing impact at that instant. Minor ambiguity with a late slide stop exists, but timing favors the release.

action_sounds.description: The follow-through pose itself generates no sound; the later ball roll and pin crash stem from the ball, not the held finish.
action_sounds.evidence: After release, audio remains ambient until the rolling/pin sounds at ~7.2-8.5 s, which are not attributable to the bowler's pose.

action_sounds.description: Possible shuffling footfalls as he pivots and walks back (~8.1-8.5 s), but the same window carries pin-impact clatter/reverberation, leaving the source ambiguous.
action_sounds.evidence: The 7.24-8.52 s burst mixes roll/pin sounds with any turn steps; frames show the turn beginning ~8.1 s, so footfalls cannot be cleanly separated from the pin-crash tail.

Ball rolling rumble building to the pin impact clatter/dull thud (~7.7-8.1 s) as the ball reaches the deck on the left-side lane; not tied to a candidate bowler action.

uncertainties: The 5.16-5.36 s tap could conceivably be a late slide-foot stop rather than ball-lane contact, though it aligns best with release.
